name: Joanna Newsom
label: Drag City
lede: A pedal harp, a voice critics could not stop arguing about, and three records in six years that went from twelve homemade songs to a two-hour triple album.

eras.title: A five-year-old asks for a harp
eras.text: Newsom grew up in Nevada City, in California's Gold Country foothills, in a house of musicians. She went from Celtic harps to a full pedal harp, then to Mills College, a keyboard job in a San Francisco band, and two homemade CDs that reached Will Oldham.

years.h: Joanna Newsom is born in Grass Valley, California
years.p: Newsom grows up next door in Nevada City. Her father plays guitar and her mother is a classically trained pianist.

years.h: Joanna Newsom, age five, asks for harp lessons
years.p: Newsom starts on piano first, moves to small Celtic harps, and gets a full-size pedal harp in seventh grade.

years.h: Joanna Newsom plays keyboards in The Pleased
years.p: While studying composition and creative writing at Mills College, Newsom joins the San Francisco band The Pleased, alongside guitarist [[Noah Georgeson|cacf76c5-f3f2-4c35-ba0c-d3f2a07c3949]]. She drops out of Mills to make music full time.

years.h: Walnut Whales: Joanna Newsom's first homemade CD
years.p: A self-recorded, self-released harp-and-voice EP. Several of its songs are rerecorded two years later for The Milk-Eyed Mender.

years.h: Joanna Newsom guests on the Nervous Cop album
years.p: Newsom plays harp on Nervous Cop's self-titled record, a project with [[Zach Hill|df6a1106-6caf-465b-bcfd-0b80d2b53516]] of [[Hella|1ecbc7e5-6e33-4062-997d-abc550dd63e6]] and [[Greg Saunier|2ae4e9b4-9e8b-4a98-920d-4f3a881dac96]] of [[Deerhoof|11eabe0c-2638-4808-92f9-1dbd9c453429]].

years.h: Will Oldham hears Yarn and Glue and calls Drag City
years.p: Newsom's second homemade EP reaches [[Will Oldham|eb51090c-662a-47a1-967c-c63292d9831a]], who recommends her to Drag City. The Chicago label signs her.
years.xp: Drag City still lists both homemade EPs, Walnut Whales and Yarn and Glue, in Newsom's discography as self-released CDs. Oldham, who records for the label as [[Bonnie 'Prince' Billy|7b0a63b2-b8e8-490e-b724-1d30cb5edfe3]], was the connection.

eras.title: A voice that split rooms
eras.text: The Milk-Eyed Mender arrived with no chart placing and a voice that split rooms: listeners either fell for it or couldn't stand it. It kept selling anyway, past 200,000 copies, and Newsom spent the next two years on the road.

years.h: The Milk-Eyed Mender comes out on Drag City
years.p: Twelve songs of harp, harpsichord and Wurlitzer, produced by her Pleased bandmate [[Noah Georgeson|cacf76c5-f3f2-4c35-ba0c-d3f2a07c3949]]. Newsom wrote all of it except the traditional Appalachian ballad Three Little Babes.
years.xp:
Georgeson also plays guitar and sings backup. The record never charted, but Wikipedia puts its U.S. sales above 200,000 copies. Pitchfork later ranked it No. 47 among the best albums of the 2000s.

The songs kept traveling. [[Bombay Bicycle Club|0ae49abe-d6af-44fa-8ab0-b9ace5690e6f]] covered Swansea, and [[The Roots|80b3cf5e-18fe-4c59-98c7-e5bb87210710]] built their 2010 track Right On around The Book of Right-On.

years.h: Sprout and the Bean gets its own CD single
years.p: Drag City issues the opening song of The Milk-Eyed Mender as a CD5, catalog DC287, with its own video.

years.h: Joanna Newsom and Bill Callahan become a couple
years.p: Newsom dates [[Bill Callahan|c309d914-93af-4b3f-8058-d79c75ea89da]], the Drag City songwriter who records as [[Smog|89af9575-4d72-4345-8eba-e9de3d36ac34]]. Wikipedia dates the relationship from 2004 to 2007.

eras.title: Five songs, fifty-five minutes
eras.text: For the follow-up Newsom went the other way: five long songs, a full orchestra arranged by Van Dyke Parks, harp and voice cut to tape by Steve Albini, a mix by Jim O'Rourke. According to Wikipedia, the songs deal with the sudden death of her best friend, a continuing illness and a tumultuous relationship.

years.h: Steve Albini records Joanna Newsom's harp and voice in LA
years.p: Newsom and [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] track Ys at Village Recording Studio in Los Angeles, all analog, on two 24-track machines.

years.h: Van Dyke Parks adds an orchestra to Ys
years.p: [[Van Dyke Parks|74be7080-080f-49d0-b8c5-1166eed1bb8e]], who made Song Cycle in 1967, co-produces and arranges orchestra for four of the five songs at Entourage Studios.
years.xp: Tim Boyle recorded the orchestra. [[Jim O'Rourke|172aab84-4c01-4dc0-b2ad-e723033e10ec]] mixed the album, and it was mastered at Abbey Road. Wikipedia lists Parks' Song Cycle and Roy Harper's 1971 Stormcock as models.

years.cap: Ys cover: a painted portrait of Newsom by Benjamin Vierling
years.h: Ys: five songs, 55 minutes, one of them nearly 17
years.p: Named for a sunken city of Breton legend, Ys runs Emily, Monkey & Bear, Sawdust & Diamonds, Only Skin and Cosmia. Pitchfork gives it 9.4 and it enters the Billboard 200 at No. 134, her first U.S. chart entry.
years.xp:
Newsom's sister Emily sings on Emily. [[Bill Callahan|c309d914-93af-4b3f-8058-d79c75ea89da]] sings backup on Only Skin, which runs 16 minutes and 53 seconds.

By March 2010, Ys had sold more than 250,000 copies, according to Wikipedia. It was nominated for the 2007 Shortlist Music Prize.

years.h: The shortest song on Ys runs over seven minutes
years.p: The shortest song on Ys, Cosmia, runs 7 minutes and 15 seconds. The longest, Only Skin, runs almost 17.
years.xp: After twelve short songs on The Milk-Eyed Mender, Newsom handed Drag City an album of five, with a 12-minute opener. Critics who had called her first record a novelty mostly came around: Metacritic's average for Ys is 85.

years.h: Joanna Newsom & The Ys Street Band EP
years.p: Drag City catalog DC336. Newsom's touring band plays the new song Colleen alongside reworked older material.
play: Joanna Newsom and the Ys Street Band

years.h: Joanna Newsom and Bill Callahan split
years.p: Wikipedia dates the end of Newsom's relationship with [[Bill Callahan|c309d914-93af-4b3f-8058-d79c75ea89da]] to 2007.

eras.title: Losing the voice, making three discs
eras.text: Midway through the next record Newsom's voice gave out. Vocal cord nodules kept her silent for two months, and the singing that came back was lower, rounder and less sharp-edged. The record it went into was a triple album.

years.h: Vocal cord nodules silence Joanna Newsom for two months
years.p: Newsom develops nodules on her vocal cords and cannot speak for two months. Instrumental work on the new album keeps going while vocal tracking stops.
years.xp: The recovery changed how she sang. Wikipedia notes the difference is audible on Have One on Me, which had been partly sung before the nodules and was finished after.

years.cap: Have One on Me, Drag City DC390
years.h: Have One on Me: 18 songs, three discs, 124 minutes
years.p: Recorded in 2009 at studios from Weed, California, to Berkeley to New York, mixed in Los Angeles and Tokyo. It peaks at No. 75 on the Billboard 200.
years.xp:
[[Ryan Francesconi|88bdf861-1561-4bfd-8bc2-99bb5499ed11]] arranged and conducted, and [[Neal Morgan|99df250f-7065-4bb5-ae31-7bd6a7ca2b83]] arranged the drums and percussion. [[Jim O'Rourke|172aab84-4c01-4dc0-b2ad-e723033e10ec]] and [[Noah Georgeson|cacf76c5-f3f2-4c35-ba0c-d3f2a07c3949]] mixed it.

Pitchfork gave it 9.2. Songs include Good Intentions Paving Company, Baby Birch and '81.

years.h: The Roots build Right On around a Joanna Newsom song
years.p: [[The Roots|80b3cf5e-18fe-4c59-98c7-e5bb87210710]] sample and rework Newsom's The Book of Right-On for Right On, on their 2010 album How I Got Over.

years.h: What We Have Known, a Joanna Newsom 12-inch single
years.p: Drag City issues What We Have Known on 12-inch vinyl, catalog DC287V.

eras.title: A wedding, a narrator, and Divers
eras.text: Newsom married, stepped into film work for Paul Thomas Anderson, and spent years building a fourth album. Divers came with Anderson's video and became her first No. 1 on a Billboard chart.

years.h: Joanna Newsom marries Andy Samberg in Big Sur
years.p: Newsom marries comedian Andy Samberg of Saturday Night Live and The Lonely Island in Big Sur, California.

years.cap: Joanna Newsom at Greensboro College, 2006 · Wikimedia
years.h: Joanna Newsom narrates Inherent Vice
years.p: In Paul Thomas Anderson's Thomas Pynchon adaptation, Newsom plays Sortilège and narrates the film. Critics single out the narration.
years.xp: It wasn't her first screen work: she had already turned up in the sketch show Portlandia. Anderson would direct her next music video the following year.

years.h: Paul Thomas Anderson directs the Sapokanikan video
years.p: Newsom announces Divers with the single Sapokanikan and a Paul Thomas Anderson video shot around New York. The clip later screens on her tour.

years.h: Divers opens at No. 1 on Billboard's Alternative chart
years.p: Arrangements by [[Nico Muhly|cd9e43ec-12dc-4567-9c60-1e554164cf05]] (Anecdotes), [[David Longstreth|cf8a8d1c-fa71-4582-ab64-c63e42c8a11d]] of [[Dirty Projectors|71a94ed8-03cc-459a-bd35-a081ca88a402]] (Time, As a Symptom) and [[Ryan Francesconi|88bdf861-1561-4bfd-8bc2-99bb5499ed11]]. Its first week, 14,000 units, is her best start.
years.xp:
[[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] engineered, and [[Noah Georgeson|cacf76c5-f3f2-4c35-ba0c-d3f2a07c3949]] co-produced and mixed. The City of Prague Philharmonic Orchestra plays on it.

Pitchfork called it a love letter in the form of a reckoning with death. Metacritic's average is 88, her highest.

eras.title: New songs, sung in cemeteries and opening slots
eras.text: After Divers Newsom went quiet on record. When she came back to stages, it was with unrecorded songs, while an old collaborator's death marked how long it had been.

years.h: Joanna Newsom opens for Fleet Foxes with unreleased songs
years.p: Newsom plays surprise sets opening for [[Fleet Foxes|fa97dd36-1b82-43d7-a6e4-2adeafd59cef]], debuting new songs including Bombs Are Whistling and Marie at the Mill.

years.h: Steve Albini, engineer of Ys and Divers, dies at 61
years.p: [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] dies of a heart attack in Chicago. He had recorded Newsom's harp and voice for Ys and engineered Divers.

years.h: Joanna Newsom plays a Hollywood Forever residency
years.p: At Hollywood Forever Cemetery in Los Angeles, Newsom premieres more new songs across a short run of shows.

years.h: Nevada City declares Joanna Newsom Day
years.p: The Gold Country town where Newsom grew up gives her a day of her own.
